text:
devon_client: hey team — embeddings endpoint started returning 400s for us around 10:02 UTC and our token usage shot way up. created a quick repro below, can you help?

sara_support: sorry to hear that — can you paste the exact request body (no keys) and any error body you got?

devon_client: pasted — we were trying to send a single precomputed vector but our client wraps it. payload: ```json
{
  "model": "embed-lite-1536",
  "input": [[0.001, 0.12, 0.34, 0.56 /* ...1536 floats total... */]]
}
```
error: ```json
{
  "error": "400 Bad Request",
  "message": "embedding payload shape mismatch: expected list-of-vectors (N x D) but got nested-array depth 3"
}
```

sara_support: thanks. two quick things we see a lot: (1) double-wrapping arrays (you sent a batch containing a batch), and (2) aggressive retry loops that multiply requests when the client gets 4xx/5xx. both can cause spike in tokens billed and throughput throttles.

alex_engineer: quick repro note from infra: the runtime validated shape and returned 400 early, but the client retried 20x in 30s which triggered rate-limiter + billing. can you share the client code that builds the payload?

devon_client: using our JS client helper: ```js
const vec = new Float32Array(1536); // filled earlier
await fetch('/v1/embeddings', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Authorization: `Bearer ${KEY}` },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'embed-lite-1536', input: [vec] })
});
```

sara_support: aha — JSON.stringify on a Float32Array produces an object that the server sees as nested array-ish, and wrapping it in [vec] is turning into a double-nested payload after serialization. two immediate fixes: (A) send a plain Array: 
```js
body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'embed-lite-1536', input: [Array.from(vec)] })
```
or (B) if sending a single vector, use the top-level list correctly: 
```js
body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'embed-lite-1536', input: Array.from(vec) }) // if API expects one vector without extra nesting
```
Pick the variant that matches your caller (single vector vs batch of vectors).

devon_client: ok that explains it. we thought input: [vec] would be safe. client libs hide Float32Array weirdness.

alex_engineer: we'll add a defensive server error that gives a clearer hint, but client-side change is fastest. also set exponential backoff on retries so a 400 doesn't become 20x requests.

jenna_billing: tagging billing. @devon_client I can review the spike once you confirm the window (10:02–10:06 UTC) and whether you accepted retries. If it's caused by our SDK bug we can consider crediting.

devon_client: thanks — confirmed window 1797654321–1797654550, and we were running a custom retry wrapper.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-4571 — embeddings 400-retry-billing-spike. assigned to eng/infra.

alex_engineer: followups: (1) can you try the Array.from(vec) change and paste a curl that works for you? (2) upgrade SDK to v1.2.3 — we shipped a fix that serializes TypedArrays to normal arrays.

devon_client: tested with Array.from(vec) — request now returns 200 and embedding ID. working example: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"embed-lite-1536","input":[[0.001,0.12,0.34,0.56 /* ... */]]}'
```

sara_support: great. next steps: we'll have infra add a clearer 400 message like "input shape: double nested arrays detected, please send list-of-vectors; see support doc link". jenna will look at billing. alex will land SDK fix to avoid accidental Float32Array serialization.

jenna_billing: noted — I'll reconcile the usage spikes and follow up in this thread with potential credit. expect update within 2 business days.

devon_client: appreciate it. learned to validate payload shape locally before sending. thanks all :thumbsup:

sara_support: closing loop — please reopen if anything else pops up. ```
